title: A Asset for the Border Again
premise: August Nystrom, a whistle-blower hiding under four identities in a Baltic border town, spots a passenger flight on radar that every database insists never existed. Chasing the ghost flight, he uncovers a state-sponsored rendition program and realizes his own extraction contact is embedded in it. To expose the truth and save the flight's still-living passengers, he must surrender his final proof of the original incident that destroyed his life, trading his last leverage for strangers' lives. The book ends with August boarding the dawn extraction under a fifth name, anonymous again but finally able to sleep, having mailed the secret to a journalist he'll never meet.
about_author: Sebastian Dravenmoor is the pseudonym of a former logistics analyst who spent a decade writing border-region reports no one read until one of them mattered too much. He writes thrillers from a coastal town he declines to name, about people who trade names the way others trade currency.

chapters.title: The Flight That Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV August Nystrom. Insomniac August, monitoring air traffic as a nightly ritual, logs a passenger flight that vanishes from every tracker mid-air. When he cross-references the callsign, he finds his own old case number buried in its manifest metadata. The beat is cold dread: the past he buried has wings.

chapters.title: Four Names, No Alibis
chapters.summary: POV August. August works his network of smugglers and archivists to reconstruct the ghost flight's route, but each query burns an identity as someone starts closing in. His handler, Ilse, warns him to stop, yet her denials are too precise. The beat is paranoia tightening: invisibility is revealed as a debt, not a refuge.

chapters.title: The Extraction Ledger
chapters.summary: POV August. August breaks into a decommissioned airfield hangar and finds the rendition program's ledger, which lists the ghost flight's passengers as alive and detained, and names Ilse as its architect. Caught by the program's fixer, he bargains: the ledger for the passengers' release. The beat is the climax, a moral pivot where leverage becomes a weapon he chooses to disarm.

chapters.title: Dawn, Fifth Name
chapters.summary: POV August. At the airfield at first light, August mails the ledger to a journalist, watches the detained passengers walk free, and confronts Ilse one last time before boarding his extraction. He sheds his fourth name at the gate. The beat is quiet resolution: justice delivered outside the law, and the first full night's sleep in years.
